title: Two ways to compare
objective: Compare quantities, explain a representation and revise a claim. Synthetic beta practice; no learner data.
materials: Paper or the offline response sheet
steps: Choose counters, drawing, oral explanation or typed answers.
Represent each group; check a claim using your representation.
Explain a choice and try a different arrangement.
adaptations: Read the prompts aloud or let the adult transcribe a stated answer. Name this support.
Use 3 and 4 first, or extend by finding another pair with a difference of 2.

items.prompt: Group A has 5 counters. Group B has 7. Which has more, and how many more? Explain with a drawing or matching.
items.answer: B has 2 more. Accept matching, drawing or spoken reasoning showing the difference.
items.rationale: One point for B; one for a justified difference of 2. State any counting or transcription support.

items.prompt: An AI says: moving the 5 counters farther apart makes more counters. Check the claim.
items.answer: Spacing changes; the count stays 5. Accept a recount or one-to-one demonstration.
items.rationale: One point for rejecting the claim; one for observable checking. A bare yes/no is partial evidence.

items.prompt: Show two different arrangements of 7 counters. What changed and what stayed the same?
items.answer: Many arrangements are valid. The total remains 7. Invite an explanation and a revision; do not rate creativity or personality.
items.rationale: Optional criteria only: one for two arrangements, one for explaining invariant total. Prefer descriptive feedback when the response is exploratory.
